#### Stage 3C.7 Summary — Prior-Cache and Residual Joint Rescue

##### Outcome

Stage 3C.7 is **technically PASS (20/20)** on all 24 frozen primary base problems. The target-specific scientific outcome is:

- **Target A: O2 — Residual–Cache Complementarity.** The frozen L33 `h_post_attn` residual and L34–35 downstream `t_pre` cache jointly recover the deficit substantially and near-completely.
- **Target B: O1 — Prior-Cache Carrier.** Full P4 `t_pre` K+V exactly restores the native score, but the frozen L35 residual plus L35-only downstream cache remains below the substantial-joint threshold.
- Overall: **target-heterogeneous O2-A / O1-B**.

The sole review-only recommendation is **GO — Token-Type Carrier Atlas**. No follow-on experiment was started.

##### Frozen design and validation

The exact Stage 3C.6 seven-base validation and 24-base primary cohorts, Target A/B states, P4 target-ROI suppression (layers 16–35, all 32 logical heads, `t_pre` only), semantic O/C conditions, and A5000 numerical environment were reused. Donors and recipients always shared the same image condition.

Cache patches use the native Qwen3-VL GQA representation: post-RoPE K and projected V with shape `[1, 8 KV heads, 1 t_pre token, 128]`. Only `t_pre` was replaced. Visual prompt K/V, current-query K/V, and every other reasoning-cache position remained recipient-native. The frozen joint scopes were A: L33 `h_post_attn` + L34–35 cache; B: L35 `h_pre` + L35 cache.

The corrected one-base smoke and all seven validation bases passed cache layout, position, component isolation, visual/current-state invariance, exact self-patch, exact Stage 3C.6 reproduction, joint-order, repeatability, and finite-score checks. A first smoke launch that accidentally inherited two Slurm tasks was preserved as `raw/validation_smoke_failed_v1` and excluded before audit; the rerun fixed only the launch task count.

##### Phase A — prior-cache rescue

| Target | K median gain / RR | V median gain / RR | K+V median gain / RR | Classification |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A | -0.0829 / -0.1393 | 0.3638 / 0.6404 | 0.5528 / 1.0000 | C-KV |
| B | -0.0192 / -0.0892 | 0.2047 / 0.6000 | 0.3035 / 1.0000 | C-KV |

K-only rescue is not robust for either target. V-only rescue is robust for both, but its median gain is only about two-thirds of K+V and does not meet the frozen “approaches K+V” rule. K+V exceeds both K and V robustly after target-specific 12-test Holm correction, yielding C-KV for both targets.

Full P4 K+V exactly reproduces the native token-level scores in **96/96** target × condition × base cells. Thus the matching native `t_pre` cache is sufficient to repair the tested P4 deficit under this intervention. This does not make RR a unique causal information fraction.

Suppression-induced cache deltas begin after layer 16, as expected because the layer-16 K/V projection precedes its local suppressed attention output. Delta magnitude was never used to choose layers. Its post-freeze Spearman association with full-cache rescue was 0.446 for A and 0.643 for B; this is secondary and descriptive.

##### Phase B — residual and cache joint rescue

| Target | Residual RR | Downstream-cache RR | Joint RR | Frozen joint gate | Outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| A | 0.4162 | 0.6902 | 1.0006 | substantial + near-complete | O2 |
| B | 0.3410 | 0.1083 | 0.4611 | below 0.50 | O1 |

For A, joint gain exceeds residual-only on 24/24 bases (median increment 0.3051) and downstream-cache-only on 20/24 bases (median increment 0.1192); both pass the fixed Holm family and robustness rule. This is clean residual–cache complementarity at the frozen boundary. It is not labeled O3 synergy because downstream cache alone is already substantial.

For B, L35 downstream-cache-only and joint-over-residual each have only 16/24 positive bases and fail the 75% robustness rule. Joint RR is 0.4611, below 0.50. Yet full P4 cache rescue is exact, locating B's tested cache support more broadly than the one remaining downstream layer at its L35 boundary.

The Target-A-only gated joint decomposition passed mechanical validation and all 24 bases: K+residual median gain/RR is 0.1939/0.4349 and is not robust because its bootstrap mean CI crosses zero; V+residual is robust at 0.4940/0.7265; K+V+residual is 0.5724/1.0006 and exceeds both. The gated mechanism is Value-dominant with additional K/V interaction. Target B was not run because its J4 gate failed.

##### Controls and reproducibility

- Stage 3C.6 native, suppressed, and frozen residual-only scores reproduce exactly for every primary target/condition cell.
- Native→native and suppressed→suppressed cache/residual self patches are exact on all seven validation bases.
- Q/prompt cache replacement is exactly equal to suppressed in 96/96 primary cells; mean and median gain are zero.
- J5 full-cache + residual is exactly native in 96/96 cells.
- Corrected smoke J4 repeats are exact. Validation and primary mechanical audits pass.
- Maximum GPU allocation across primary runs was 8.83 GiB. Optional rollouts were prospectively omitted.

##### Interpretation and limits

The exact immediately preceding reasoning token's native K/V cache carries behaviorally useful consequences of the P4 visual-acquisition event in both frozen targets. Target A additionally demonstrates that native late current residual and continued native prior-cache access are complementary. Target B instead needs cache restoration across the broader P4 depth to obtain complete rescue under the tested suffix readout.

This result is conditional on two frozen evidence coordinates, localized numeric MathVerse edits, teacher-forced suffix scoring, and an intervention that replaces native state. It does not establish universal token-type roles, whole-history lifecycle, attention-sink function, upstream vision origin, failure mechanisms, or a unique information decomposition. Raw attention was neither a selection signal nor an intervention target.

##### Stop boundary

Stage 3C.7 stops here. No Token-Type Carrier Atlas, sink manipulation, R_last2/R_last4, residual-feature analysis, Stage 4, multi-evidence refresh, or failure experiment has started.

#### Stage 3C.8 Summary — Token-Type Carrier Atlas

##### Outcome

Stage 3C.8 is **technically PASS (25/25)**. The fresh 64-base primary cohort supports a combined **O4 recency-dominant / O6 phase-specific carrier taxonomy**, with a narrower O1-like later-coordinate visual-entity effect. The result does not support a general punctuation-boundary claim, and the planned long-horizon Phase D extension was infeasible under its prospectively frozen cohort gate.

The sole review-only recommendation is **CONDITIONAL GO — Dedicated Long-Horizon Causal-Checkpoint Cohort**. No later experiment was started.

##### Cohort and frozen design

The prospective screen preserved 105/240 attempted fresh outcomes: 82 completed-correct and 23 wrong. Eighty-two correct candidates were reviewed, 75 edits were constructed, 11 construction attempts were rejected, and exactly 64 fully valid unique bases were retained. Selection used neither attention nor carrier effects. The 8-base mechanical set, exact 24 Stage 3C.7 historical anchors, and 64 fresh bases were disjoint for fresh inference. The frozen annotation set contains 31,682 token rows and 29,077 lexical spans.

The model, A5000 environment, seed 1234, native GQA K/V layout, P4 `t_pre`, Phase-B T16 suppression, and Phase-C generation-start cutoff were inherited exactly. All eight validation bases passed position/group selectivity, visual/current-query invariance, T16 and cutoff semantics, self-patches, repeatability, and finite-score checks. Peak allocated GPU memory across primary runs was 9.03 GiB.

##### Phase A — immediate prior-token carrier

All 24 historical anchors reproduced Stage 3C.7 exactly. On the fresh cohort, all-layer `t_pre` K+V rescue was robust at both evidence coordinates:

| Coordinate | N positive | Median gain | Mean gain | Bootstrap mean 95% CI |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A-like | 64/64 | 1.125 | 1.669 | [1.225, 2.171] |
| B-like | 57/64 | 0.151 | 0.278 | [0.190, 0.381] |

V restoration was broadly positive, whereas K alone was weak or negative overall. This establishes a strong immediate prior-token cache carrier under the tested suppression, not a unique information fraction.

##### Phase B — recent reasoning carrier atlas

Rescue was sharply localized by recency. For A-like readout, distance-1 K+V was robust (64/64 positive; median 2.382) and distance-2 K+V remained robust (56/64; median 0.125); distances 4–16 were null. For B-like readout, distance-1 K+V was robust (60/64; median 0.296); distance-2 V was robust, while distance-2 K+V missed the 75% directionality rule; distances 4–16 were null. The all-recent median rescue ratio was 0.478, below the frozen 0.50 sub-gate.

After within-base recency matching, `FUNCTION_WORD` was robust at the A-like coordinate, while `VISUAL_ENTITY` and `TARGET_ALIGNED` were robust at the B-like coordinate. Thus distance is the dominant global structure, but semantic alignment adds coordinate-specific information after recency control. This does not make every entity token a privileged carrier.

##### Phase C — prompt/question carrier atlas

The mandatory full-Q positive reference was robust: 61/64 positive, median gain 0.624, mean 1.514, bootstrap mean 95% CI [1.111, 1.949]. Exhaustive single-position, lexical-span, group, and structural-control outputs were retained for all 88 historical/fresh bases.

Two K+V groups passed the frozen Phase-C class gate. `NUMERIC_LITERAL` transfer was primarily K-associated (K median 0.156, 55/64 positive; V median 0.064, 45/64). `PUNCTUATION` transfer was primarily V-associated (V median 0.062, 49/64; K median 0.021, 37/64). The decomposition was run only after the K+V gate froze those two classes.

The punctuation group should not be interpreted as boundary-specific evidence integration: punctuation was weaker than its within-base nearest prompt controls (median difference -0.016; 21/64 positive). Target-aligned prompt positions had a positive but heterogeneous matched difference (median 0.010; 29/51 positive) and did not meet the frozen 75% robustness rule. Prompt and late-reasoning carrier taxonomies therefore differ.

##### Phase D gate

The Phase A/B carrier-signal gate opened, but only 15 fresh bases met the independently frozen requirement of at least 128 pre-`E_d` tokens and two reasoning segments, below the minimum 28. Phase D inference, necessity tests, and route controls were not run; explicit manifests and derived outputs are empty. This is a feasibility result, not evidence that long-horizon causal checkpoints do not exist.

##### Cross-stage interpretation and limits

Stages 2A–2C showed that ROI attention is often mention-centered and cannot identify acquisition. Stage 3A established pre-mention visual-content sensitivity, and Stages 3B–3C.7 localized useful consequences into residual/cache states. Stage 3C.8 now shows that those consequences are carried differently across lifecycle phases: strongly by the immediately preceding reasoning state, locally by recent tokens with target-dependent semantic structure, and in the prompt by numeric/punctuation groups with distinct K/V profiles.

These conclusions are conditional on localized numeric MathVerse edits, two evidence-coordinate readouts, teacher-forced scoring, native-state transplantation, and Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking. Raw attention was not used for cohort, token, span, gate, or carrier selection. Rescue ratios are unclipped and are not unique causal information fractions. The atlas does not establish sink causality, a universal token taxonomy, or repeated long-horizon checkpoints.

##### Stop boundary

Stage 3C.8 stops here. No sink manipulation, unconstrained history search, residual-feature learning, Stage 4, multi-evidence refresh, or failure analysis was started.

#### A6000 Platform Calibration Summary

##### Decision

**FAIL — A6000 PLATFORM NOT READY (F1 scoring-path parity failure).** Stage 3C.9 restart is not authorized.

This is an implementation/methods result, not a scientific finding about the model or hardware.

##### What was frozen before scoring

The hardware migration amendment, 12-base historical cohort, four-device pool, software/model configuration, and `1e-5` token/aggregate parity tolerances were persisted before any A6000 calibration score. The partial A5000 Stage 3C.9 screen remains provenance-only and was not mixed into this calibration.

##### Risk-first Layer A result

Base 74 was run first on A6000 GPU UUID `GPU-d2516130-3b52-5a2b-afd5-77efd3c612c1` with three deterministic repeats in original and counterfactual image conditions.

- Deterministic full-path replay: passed for native, source-suppressed, and K+V rescue scores and captured states.
- Full-path K-only, V-only, K+V, and residual self patches: passed in native→native and suppressed→suppressed controls.
- Architecture: 36 language layers, 32 logical query heads, 8 KV heads, 4 query heads per KV group, head dimension 128.
- All executed scores: finite.
- Peak allocated GPU memory: 9,150,241,792 bytes.

The mandatory parity gate failed. Across original/counterfactual conditions and native/suppressed/KV-rescue paths, full-versus-bounded differences ranged from `0.0203` to `2.9393` in aggregate D and from `0.1481` to `8.8680` in token log probability, far above `1e-5`.

##### Focused diagnosis

A single predeclared follow-up compared full recomputation, the historical one-shot cache path, and streaming cache paths on the same frozen base.

- One-shot cache versus full also failed: aggregate |ΔD| was `0.0998` (O) and `0.0342` (C).
- Streaming chunk-size sensitivity was nonzero: aggregate |ΔD| was `0.1018` (O) and `0.000042` (C) between full-prefix and one-token chunks.
- This reproduces the already documented Stage 3B.0 observation that BF16 full and cached execution use different matrix shapes and are deterministic but not numerically identical.

Thus the result does not support a simple stochastic-device or token-coordinate failure. It does show that the current frozen `1e-5` full/cache equivalence criterion is not met by the existing BF16 implementation.

##### Stop handling

The plan's F1 rule says to stop before Stage 3C.9 and fix scoring implementation. Therefore Layers B, C, and D were not run; their required paths contain explicit `NOT_RUN` records. No device pool was accepted, no cross-hardware scientific continuity claim was made, and Stage 3C.9 was not restarted.

##### Required next decision

The next action needs review because it would amend the calibration design. The cleanest candidate is to define all Stage 3C.9 causal contrasts against matched recipient/source baselines within one fixed cached/chunked execution path, then prospectively validate deterministic replay, self-patch exactness, selectivity, and chunking sensitivity. Another option is a different scoring implementation that genuinely matches full recomputation under the frozen dtype. Neither change was made here.

</details>

#### Stage 3C.9 — Dedicated Long-Horizon Causal Checkpoints

##### Outcome

Stage 3C.9 technical status: **PASS (20/20)**. Mechanical validation: **16/16**. The primary independent unit is `base_problem_id`.

##### Prospective cohort

- Raw trajectories attempted: 600 (correct 391, wrong 207, truncated 2, invalid 0).
- Frozen primary cohort: 48 unique bases; disjoint mechanical validation: 8 bases.
- Every retained base has exactly three score-blind semantic events (first, midpoint-nearest, and last in annotation order), at least two separated by 24 tokens, frozen local/final readouts, a validated semantic edit quartet, and a manually validated ROI mapping.
- Evidence types: localized_angle_label=27, localized_formula_label=2, localized_length_label=16, localized_radius_label=3.

##### Event-local visual-source sensitivity

Both W8 and W16 were prospectively evaluated across all 36 language layers and all 32 logical heads. 29 frozen events were source-sensitive under at least one tested window. A non-sensitive result means only “source-insensitive under the tested W8/W16 target-ROI windows”; it does not establish non-visual reasoning.

##### Causal checkpoint rescue

There were 2 C2/C3 event spans. C2/C3 required a same-window visual-source deficit, positive sign-aligned native K+V span rescue in both O and C, mean rescue at least 0.05 nats/candidate-token, median unclipped rescue ratio at least 0.25, and event-span rescue greater than its predeclared matched neighbor. Constituent-token scores were secondary and never redefined a span.

##### Repeated formation and lifetime

0/48 bases met `REPEATED_CHECKPOINT` (at least two non-overlapping C2/C3 spans separated by at least 24 reasoning tokens). Lifetime phenotypes among confirmed checkpoints: {'L-Short': 2}; same-evidence pairs classified as L-Replaced: 0. Only independently annotated semantic readouts were used; no arbitrary pseudo-readouts were introduced.

##### Route decomposition

Phase D did not run: 0 bases met the two-checkpoint pair gate versus 16 required. This is a gated feasibility result, not evidence that direct or inherited routes are absent.

##### Enrichment and heterogeneity

Checkpoint lexical/reasoning-role summaries were computed only after causal classes froze. Raw token-type counts are not treated as enrichment evidence; matched controls preserve progress, span length, local density, and boundary context where available. Event and target heterogeneity remains visible in `analysis/target_heterogeneity.json`.

##### Scientific boundaries and limitations

- Attention did not select cohorts, events, spans, windows, or route pairs, and no attention/sink intervention was run.
- Source suppression is a necessity assay under a specific ROI/window, so redundancy can mask relevance.
- Span rescue identifies sufficiency of the tested frozen K/V checkpoint representation, not a unique carrier or exclusive route.
- Rescue ratios are descriptive, unclipped, and are not unique information fractions.
- A post-hoc validity audit found material Phase-A-versus-Phase-B source-score instability for the 33 rescored event-windows (median absolute per-condition difference 0.12363; 24/33 source gates changed at the frozen 0.05 threshold). Same-path replay remains exact, but the exact nominal checkpoint count is path-sensitive.
- The stable sensitivity result is 0 repeated-checkpoint bases at effect floors 0.025, 0.05, 0.10, and 0.15. Base 38 supplies direct long-horizon evidence for a short-lived checkpoint; base 149 has no distinct downstream/final readout, so its automated `L-Short` label is right-censored.
- Stages 2A–3C.8 must be considered jointly before acting on the single recommendation below.

##### Recommendation

**EXPAND_CONFIRMED_CHECKPOINT_PAIR_YIELD:** Review the confirmed local checkpoints and resolve the documented cross-phase score-stability issue before designing any score-blind cohort expansion intended to increase independent separated checkpoint pairs.

Stage 3C.9 stops here. No sink-causality, residual-feature, unconstrained-history, Stage 4, multi-evidence, or failure-analysis experiment was started.

On the unchanged 48-base, 144-event cohort, 33 events were source-sensitive in at least one frozen window. There were **10 distinct C2/C3 checkpoints** and **0/48 repeated-checkpoint bases**. Classes: {'C0': 111, 'C1': 23, 'C2': 9, 'C3': 1}.

All 288 mechanically valid W8/W16 event-window pairs received native, suppressed, event-span rescue and equal-width neighbor rescue in O/O_sham/C/C_sham before classification (576 raw condition files). No cohort, span, ROI, candidate suffix or readout changed.

#### Stage 3C.10 — Reasoning-State Retrieval Trigger

**Technical PASS; O1 — Reasoning-State Retrieval Trigger at both targets. M2 — Routing mediation only.**

Recent reasoning contribution causally changes target-specific current-query visual-source dependence at the two historical retrieval coordinates. The stronger claim that this behavioral effect is mediated by the frozen late Q geometry is **not supported**. All-head native-Q rescue restores routing exactly but does not robustly rescue VSD; the optional late h_pre rescue is also nonrobust.

The approved plan is complete and stopped. The sole recommendation is **GO — Stage 4 Multi-Evidence Retrieval/Refresh**, for review only. No follow-on experiment has started.

##### Fixed assay and validity

Exact Stage 3C.3 manifests: 7 validation and 24 primary bases, with M/T and A/B paired within each base. Original O images, model/tokenizer, historical divergent suffixes, ROIs, causal/noncausal heads, and question-text source spans are preserved. A uses upstream layers 0–28 and routing layer 29; B uses 0–27 and layer 28. All 32 query heads receive trigger deletion. T0 suppresses only the current query, all 36 layers/all 32 heads.

Every comparison uses one per-base A6000 BF16 cached partition: native multimodal prefill, maximum 2048 generated-token chunk, and shared before/after barriers at every M/T query. The RDS function is imported unchanged from Stage 3C.3. All causal denominators and controls are newly scored on this same path. Historical A5000 full-path values are descriptive references only.

Validation: 15/15 checks across seven bases, 28 state files and 517 arms. No-op, deterministic replay, self-Q, inherited uninstrumented cached scores and cached T0 are exact. Actual full-past K/V comparisons imply unchanged visual K/V. Artifact audit: 21/21 checks across 412 files, 5121 arms and 207811 source-layer traces. Focused/new plus inherited tests: 45 passed.

R16 excludes the current token and intersects generated history: primary base 119 has 14/13 preceding M tokens for A/B, and base 120 has 6/5. Validation base 128-B-M has 15. No base was excluded. E16 is available on 22/24 T bases and is never shifted to fill missing history. Q is the exact historical question-content span; structural `<|im_start|>` is untouched.

##### Primary results

Eight prespecified contrasts per target use two-sided paired Wilcoxon with Holm correction. Unrun rescue slots were p=1 when primary gates froze; those gates never changed afterward. Robust positive means corrected p<.05, positive bootstrap mean CI, median>0 and at least 75% positive bases. Bootstrap uses 10,000 base resamples, seed 12348. E16 comparisons use 22 available paired bases.

Both targets pass all five behavioral-trigger gate contrasts. R16 also exceeds the question-source control. Routing changes at all 24 T bases per target; behavioral trigger effects are positive on 20/24 A and24/24 B. Routing alone is not the basis of this conclusion.

##### Temporal and layer localization

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

Entries are median TE_VSD. k80=16 at both targets is a tested threshold descriptor, not a unique 16-token information span: A R8 and B R4 lie just below 80% of the R16 median. The B curve is nonmonotonic. Trigger influence is broader across the tested recent window than the earlier 1–2-token carrier result.

Only layers 16–23 (L2) pass the frozen bin-wise correction at both targets. A median TE_VSD=0.593875; B=0.381186. Other bins are retained as negative evidence; they were not redefined.

##### Mediation and its limits

| Target | Rescue | Median VSD gain | Positive | Corrected p | Robust |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A | All 32 Q | -0.000842544 | 12/24 | 0.508766 | False |
| A | Historical 4 Q | -0.00456686 | 11/24 | 1 | False |
| A | h_pre (secondary) | -0.224981 | 9/24 | 0.0460644 | False |
| B | All 32 Q | 0.046476 | 13/24 | 0.725741 | False |
| B | Historical 4 Q | 0.0483628 | 17/24 | 0.258597 | False |
| B | h_pre (secondary) | 0.0678165 | 17/24 | 0.0601797 | False |

All-head and selected-head Q rescues restore the primary routing readout exactly on 24/24 bases per target. This is expected when native Q is reinstated with unchanged visual K; behavioral VSD rescue is the nontrivial test. It fails the robust-positive rule for both targets. Target-A h_pre VSD gain is negative on average, with a two-sided corrected p below .05; it is not a positive rescue. Target-B h_pre gain is positive but nonrobust.

The optional h_pre donor can contain native upstream visual evidence and bypass part of all-layer ROI suppression. Its VSD result is not a guaranteed numerical upper bound. The mediator of the recent-input behavioral effect remains unknown; broader redundancy and earlier/multiple state paths are possible explanations, not established diagnoses. Exact same-path replay, source isolation and recipient-K/V audits pass, so no further diagnostic or rescue search was run.

##### Generic computation and secondary content

R16 changes residual/attention-output norms and candidate distributions as well as retrieval. Median original-candidate NLL changes at T are small (A 0.00136392, B -0.00185395), while counterfactual NLL changes are larger (A -1.50332, B -0.667137). Noncausal-head routing also changes, especially A; the trigger is not restricted to the historical four heads. M-state entropy shifts and complete E16/Q controls are saved in `analysis/generic_language_damage.json`. These controls support the bounded retrieval-specific contrast, not a claim of exclusively retrieval-only computation.

All 763 available last-eight single-position effects were scored after primary freeze. Last 16 annotations were copied from the attention-blind Stage 3C.8 taxonomy with exact token/position checks before position scoring. Effects are centered within exact target/state/distance and then aggregated once per base/type. A T-state mean effects are largest at distance 2, whereas B is strongest at distance 1; single-position effects do not by themselves identify the cumulative R16 mechanism. No universal token class is claimed. Historical sink mass is overlaid descriptively for 48 target/base cells; no sink token is manipulated.

##### Paper assessment and stop

Recent reasoning input changes target-specific current-query visual dependence at both frozen retrieval coordinates; the tested late Q/h_pre rescues do not establish its behavioral mediator.

The behavioral mediator remains unresolved: late Q rescue restores routing but not VSD, and the optional late h_pre rescue is also nonrobust. Sink release remains observational. These interventions already test the upstream recent-input link; sink manipulation is not necessary to establish the supported link and was not performed.

The paper now has a causal recent-input link in addition to the earlier query-routing and visual-Value/carrier results, but cannot present an end-to-end Q-mediated behavioral chain. The same late-state rescue ambiguity echoes prior routing/behavior dissociation; another unrestricted local search is not authorized. A separately reviewed multi-evidence test offers a larger test of the lifecycle’s scope.

**One recommendation: GO — Stage 4 Multi-Evidence Retrieval/Refresh.** Test whether the local mechanism extends to selecting and refreshing multiple visual facts, subject to a new approved Stage4 plan.

assay. All three primary source-selectivity tests and both switch/refresh tests
pass the complete prespecified robustness rule.36/48 bases satisfy the full W2

used throughout each fixed-history replay; this does not time-localize new-image
acquisition to A2 or simulate a natural free rollout.

##### Primary causal evidence

D is mean log probability of the original numeric candidate minus that of its
counterfactual. VSD is native D minus source-suppressed D. W2 removes the selected
ROI contribution in the last two queries, all36 layers/all32 heads, without
attention renormalization. W8 is frozen sensitivity. All arms use independent
event roots and identical maximum2048-token prefix chunks followed by eight
single-query barriers. Joint A+B is one explicit union reduction, not a sum of
separately scored effects.

Inference: paired two-sided Wilcoxon,10000 base-bootstrap resamples,seed12348,
nine-test Holm. Robust means positive median, positive mean-CI lower bound,

gate was evaluated; final results below include all nine tests. Units throughout:
nats per candidate token.

#### Stage5A: failure and attention-state taxonomy

**Technical PASS:20/20. The matched high-attention alignment/mirage hypothesis is
not confirmed.** Stage5A completes the200-base natural census,128-base causal
atlas and all feasible frozen assays. It establishes a broad source-dependence
record and13 reviewed integration-error events on7 bases. Strict alignment-only
and mirage confirmation cohorts have zero yield; their inferential comparisons
remain unrun. The sole next recommendation is a **Stage5B failure-rescue
feasibility review**, with no rescue experiment started.

The research question is whether similar visual attention can reflect semantic
alignment, causal retrieval, verification/refresh, or distinct visual failures.
The hypothesis predicts different causal and internal states at matched
attention magnitude. Semantic and causal labels were frozen before passive
features; wrong final answers never served as visual-hallucination labels.

##### Cohorts and execution

correctness balancing. It ends at screen208.210 screen positions were manually
reviewed, nine duplicate stimuli were excluded, and one further eligible reserve
was retained outside the natural cohort. All200 retained variants are Vision
Dominant; this is a selected-event MathVerse census, not exhaustive trace-error
or general multimodal population prevalence. The atlas contains63 bases with a
selected local error and65 others under the frozen fill rule. Historical anchors
remain separate:48 compatible Stage4A bases contribute144 discovery-reference
events, not fresh prevalence observations.

The fixed initial budget was800 and the maximum1400.551 exact-protocol existing
native trajectories were indexed for possible reuse. Fresh acquisition preserved

freeze: one rank finished its planned shard; three stopped between trajectories.
Unused reserves are preserved. No post-effect population expansion occurred.

All new GPU work used the existing tmux9 / Slurm108548 allocation on node07:

The source assay uses BF16, canonical2048-token streaming prefixes, eight fixed

heads. Removing selected source-value terms leaves Q/K/V and native attention
unchanged; no attention renormalization occurs. R16 removal is restricted to

##### Natural census and source evidence

The550 selected events include386 locally correct,94 incorrect,20 undecidable
and50 without an explicit visual claim.64/200 bases contain at least one selected
incorrect local claim;121/200 final answers are correct and79 wrong. Base-level
semantic categories can overlap. The atlas scores92 of the94 selected incorrect
events, covering63 of the64 affected bases. The remaining base and unresolved

The347 atlas events have216 demanded-source-dominant profiles,17 alternative
dominant,65 mixed-support,38 weak under both W2 and W8,17 broader-window-dependent,
and66 unresolved profiles. These labels overlap. Large negative effects are not
nulls. Median within-base mean VSD_T is1.2655 nats/candidate-token; median W8_T is
1.4821. There are237 X arms,267 validated I arms, and five raw M arms on four
bases. Only two M events have an independent T/M contrast; the other three
overlap. They do not yield a strict alignment-only cohort.
I controls match ROI cardinality and use reviewed background regions; they are
not ink-matched to printed labels. Their selection and exclusions are preserved.

The48 semantic bases meet the minimum48, below target64. The conservative numeric
construction was exhausted over92 eligible atlas bases:164 source proposals,

The79 accepted source assets yield85 validated event readouts. Semantic and sham
images preserve the frozen token layout; factorial edits use disjoint reviewed
source regions where available.82/85 event effects exceed absolute sham by0.05;
the median base-mean CE-minus-absolute-sham is12.8013. All48 base means are positive.
The subset chiefly covers numeric labels and cannot validate arbitrary wrong
entity bindings. Effects from editing another source on the target readout are
cross-source controls, not alternative-fact semantic readouts.

The96-base R16 subset has134/256 target trigger effects above0.05 and a median

event order was never substituted for full native history. Fixed-history image

##### Failure diagnoses and readout limits

| Operational label | Events | Bases | Confidence tiers |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| H-NR | 0 | 0 | {} |
| H-MR | 10 | 9 | {'Tier2': 10} |

| H-ST | 0 | 0 | {} |
| H-INT | 13 | 7 | {'Tier1': 5, 'Tier2': 8} |

H-INT is separate from visual hallucination. Its13 events have correct local
claims, demanded-source dependence, a wrong final answer and an explicitly
reviewed later error. An error already present before the selected event does
not qualify as its downstream error. The single H-SC example108_E1 claims CD=5
although the image says8: VSD_T=5.0000, semantic CE=6.6250 and sham shift=0.
It is a convergent extraction-error example, not a population-level class.

The10 H-MR labels are **frozen margin-based source profiles**, all Tier2. D is
the ground-truth candidate's mean log probability minus the foil's; the actual
native candidate direction is separately stored. Alternative-source dominance
on this margin does not establish that the alternative source caused the wrong
token. One saved-score validity diagnostic found only1/10 wrong-token
contributions above0.05. Alternative-source removal increases wrong-token
probability in7/10 and worsens the correct-versus-wrong margin in all10.
Two remaining positive wrong-token contributions are below0.001. Frozen labels
are preserved, but a wrong-source rescue mechanism is not inferred from them.
See the [orientation audit](<../outputs/stage5a/audit/hmr_readout_orientation_diagnostic.json>).

Zero H-NR/H-ST diagnoses do not establish their absence. H-NR needs measured
semantic null evidence; missing counterfactuals are not nulls. H-ST additionally
needs an actual prior-source history, and only four refresh opportunities were
resolved. Subtype counts inside the natural200 are ascertained lower bounds;
atlas counts are not presented as an unbiased mechanism prevalence estimate.

##### Attention confirmation and separability

Discovery-only normalization preserves source class and ROI-size buckets and
merges only adjacent progress/length buckets until eight reference ROIs are
available. The high criterion is a matched density percentile of at least0.90.
Both mass and density retain raw values, matched z scores and percentiles. The
ROI source class was prospectively normalized from the reviewed source kind;
the original base evidence type remains available. Sparse matching stays
unresolved rather than borrowing a different source class or ROI size.

211/347 atlas events have a matched target reference, including139/267 held-out
events.19 confirmation events cross the high-attention criterion. There are
zero strict mirages, zero high-attention missing-CE candidates and zero strict
alignment-only events. Alignment–retrieval and mirage–retrieval matched families
therefore have no pairs. Their six slots each remain unrun with p=1. The broad
semantic-mention/retrieval2×2 is reported separately; a mention without demanded
retrieval is not automatically a strict alignment-only mechanism.

Only grounded-correct versus locally wrong visual claims has sufficient
classifier yield. Models use fixed regularization, whole-template folds, no
base/event leakage and train-fold imputation/scaling. The confirmation data
contain76 grounded-correct and51 hallucination base/class observations, with
overlap because one base can exhibit both states. Predictions are averaged
within base/class, and bootstrap intervals resample unique bases together.

| Features | Balanced accuracy | Macro F1 | AUROC | ECE10 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| F1 | 0.843 | 0.838 | 0.908 | 0.051 |
| F2 | 0.892 | 0.887 | 0.929 | 0.070 |

F1 attention-only balanced accuracy has a base-bootstrap95% interval
[0.771, 0.908];
F5's interval is[0.879, 0.970].
These are descriptive held-out prediction results. F4/F5 contain causal features
that partly define grounded labels, so their performance is circular as
independent mechanism evidence. Feature/ROI availability and event selection can
also carry contextual information. The other three classifier tasks are
insufficient. PCA is fitted on discovery F3 and projected descriptively; clusters
do not define the taxonomy.

The two independent M candidates retain their already-scored W2 local NLL and
demanded-margin effects as descriptive evidence. Zero meet strict alignment-only
qualification, below the32-event minimum. The dedicated utility experiment,
including its distinct final-candidate margin, is unrun. Local D is not
substituted for final-answer utility.

Sink mass, t−8 release and source-group gains/losses are retained for all347
events. Matched sink confirmation has only two pairs. The sink gate is not met;
generic attention magnitude, replication and behavioral relevance are not
established. No sink manipulation occurred. Major comparisons include local and
global correctness strata and leave-one-template-out sensitivity; low yield is
reported rather than ignored.

##### Interpretation and limits

C1 uses a subset of source-editable diagrams/tables, with all 114 intact candidates reviewed independently of correctness. The target of 120 was attempted using 155 source candidates. Source editability and long-response completion are selection limits; excluded raw evidence is preserved.

C2 pairs the same image and reviewed T/X fields. A source-only revalidation during acquisition supersedes the original crop-pass metadata; whole families with prompt/ROI mismatches are excluded while raw traces are retained. Retrieval-only prompts retain spatial/ordinal cues. Task wording and expected answer lengths are not perfectly matched; this is not a claim of zero semantic alignment.

C3 opaque polygon masks remove annotated target pixels but may preserve silhouettes, context and boundary fragments. Masked yes responses are not automatically hallucinations. Translated sham shapes can also be described as additional silhouettes: target pixels are preserved, but the sham is not guaranteed neutral for object counts or shape semantics. No-image and unrelated-image final labels distinguish original source-answer consistency from presented-image truth. An explicit no combined with missing-image acknowledgement is recorded separately from verified absence; repeated no-image question text is a shared control, not independent visual evidence.

C3 final scoring uses the fixed POPE/COCO category reference. The reviewed truck/van, cup/glass, chair/stool, mattress/bed, and unrelated-image car/pickup and bowl/bucket disagreements retain unresolved local visual truth: benchmark disagreement alone does not establish an objective perception failure. These source families and their raw responses remain included.

C1 complete numeric-source prefix review covers 1766 spans across all 109 frozen eligible bases, with 235 secondary numeric ROIs. The fixed scope is the first 20 native reasoning spans, or the whole reasoning if shorter. Remaining whole-trajectory geometry is not fully annotated. Most remaining long trajectories retain unknown local truth/demand. Reviewed local claims are a limited annotation subset, so their correctness counts are not a representative accuracy estimate. Temporal prior access means an earlier reviewed source-linked utterance; it does not prove causal use.

C1 numeric regions have mixed granularity: some are coordinate or expression components, others whole expressions or table values. Numeric table keys identify data cells rather than adding separate value regions. Repeated values retain separate source identities, while ambiguous attribution remains unresolved. Region and source-claim counts therefore are not counts of independent facts. The review does not cover every glyph, geometric property or causal dependency.

Atlas matching balances count/length/edge-complexity features and dominant object categories approximately. All eligible confirmed cases are retained, including weak matches; imbalance is recorded in matching_diagnostics.json.

All matched C4 controls have original-image and complete native-text reviews under the frozen positive COCO80 presence protocol. Known out-of-scope caption errors include calling a sink a bathtub and reading Crisco as Riso. These controls are not globally error-free; see c4_natural_failure/matched_control_review.json.

Source/template folds were assigned prospectively and inherited by every condition. Exact/flagged perceptual matches stay grouped, including C3/C4 shared COCO images. Generic task instructions are shared across folds; no unseen-task-template or exhaustive historical semantic-template claim is made.

Resource totals count actual generation and replay work once, including failed mechanics and capped responses. Referenced mechanics reuse adds no compute. Device-hours exclude CPU annotation, loading and dependency waits; they are not elapsed wall time or measured utilization.

Evidence: [acceptance](<../outputs/stage6a/summaries/stage6a_acceptance.json>), [screening](<../outputs/stage6a/cohort/screening_accounting.json>), [release integrity](<../outputs/stage6a/audit/release_integrity.json>), [resources](<../outputs/stage6a/audit/resource_summary.json>), [atlas matching](<../outputs/stage6a/c4_natural_failure/matching_diagnostics.json>), [annotation integrity](<../outputs/stage6a/audit/controlled_annotation_integrity.json>).

Stage 6A stops here. No PCA, exact causal trajectory scoring, mirage confirmation, rescue or subsequent stage is executed.

##### Current Objective

##### Active Constraints

Stage6A used only the existing four RTX A6000 GPUs in Slurm109385/node03/tmux9. No new allocation or dataset download was requested. Native generation used the frozen BF16 Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking settings, seed1234, temperature .6, top-p .95, top-k20 and 40,960-token natural-EOS cap. Capped responses were retained without reruns.

Cohort membership, source/template splits, annotation truth/unknowns and the 10-pair C4 atlas remain frozen. Semantic source utterances/refreshes do not establish causal evidence use. A recommendation is not authorization for another research action.

##### Current State

The release contains 2,983 events from 1,276 bases: C1 109 bases/1,199 events; C2 31 families/124 events; C3 136 families/660 events; C4 1,000 images/events.

All 109 C1 numeric-source prefixes are reviewed: 1,766 spans and 235 secondary ROIs. The controlled annotation audit passes 1,992 events/160,285 reasoning spans, preserving all 105 baseline claims inside prefixes. Remaining geometry retains explicit unknowns. All C3 responses and the C4 labels/matched controls have the recorded manual reviews.

C1/C2/C3 construction gates pass. C4 has 10 confirmed, 50 unresolved and 940 no-detected whole-trace object-error labels in the fixed 1,000-image sample. The frozen atlas has 10 matched pairs, below the 60-pair minimum. The 1–6% protocol identification range is not a confidence interval.

Physical acquisition saved 3,182 terminal records (20 incomplete) and 13 replay generations, totaling 117.4163 measured device-hours. The primary release has 2,968 natural-EOS traces; terminal capped variants remain in its condition accounting. Device-hours are not elapsed wall time.

Summary and all 18 tables: `outputs/stage6a/summaries/stage6a_cohort_summary.md`. Release, annotation, ROI, manipulation, split, selection and resource audits are complete.

Five C1 intact cap incompletes and the four events of invalid C2 family docvqa56412 remain raw and outside the primary release. Availability gates and native-EOS feasibility are reported separately. There are no pending Stage6A acquisition or annotation tasks.

**Complete: 21/21 technical criteria pass. The broad failure-mechanism claims are not established.** All work used the existing two RTX A6000 GPUs in Slurm 110860/node 03/tmux 9; no new allocation or dataset download.

This stage tests whether visual engagement and movement track task-demanded causal evidence, and whether degraded evidence produces mirage or source-tracking failures.

W2 and W8 suppress source contributions at the last two or eight query positions. VSD measures the resulting change in the predeclared mean candidate log-probability contrast, in nats per token; it measures local source necessity rather than the time of initial acquisition.

| Completed component | Coverage |
|---|---|
| C2 factorial source assay |31 families, 124 events |
| C1 fixed-prefix stress |109 bases, 1199 condition events |
| C1 exact dynamics |20 bases, 78 anchors, 34 primary transitions, 0 matched holds, 19 selected refreshes |
| C1 native passive / geometry |1199 traces, 14906 endpoints; manual and programmatic scopes kept separate |
| C3 object stress |63 present +73 absent families, 660 native readouts |
| C4 natural validation |10 cases +10 controls, 358 endpoints including 45 predeclared wrong-claim anchors |

##### Findings

C2 focal-source necessity increases with focal demand: confirmation W2 median 1.426, 18/19 positive, Holm p=.000793; W8 median 1.063, 17/19 positive, p=.001099. The disjoint-ROI sensitivity remains positive 14/14. Expected alignment attention/QK effects and matched high-attention yield fail the full gate (only 1 eligible confirmation match). All four cells demand some visual source; this does not establish global image independence. [Evidence](<../outputs/stage6b/c2_alignment_retrieval/claim_assessment.json>).

C1 strong and mask grounding losses survive matched sham controls: held-out sham-minus-stress VSD medians 1.688 and 2.719; 57/62 and 58/62 bases are positive. All 62 confirmation bases validate the semantic counterfactual beyond render sham. There are 9 strict mirage candidates across 8/62 bases (7 independent source groups), and all 9 also collapse under W8. The post-label preferences are 4 benign and 5 error-associated; these are fixed-prefix candidate preferences, not newly generated native hallucinations. Continuous divergence does not satisfy the full 75% positive-base robustness rule, so the broad mirage claim remains unsupported. [Evidence](<../outputs/stage6b/c1_mirage/claim_assessment.json>).

Dynamics provide 9 held-out demand-aligned switches and 7 mixed comparisons in the selected transition/refresh set. The minimum panel gate fails. There is no matched-hold test of wandering, no strictly identified fixation in the selected panel, and no cohort failure-rate estimate. Selected numeric claims are correct even when geometric roles are wrong; the numeric contrast cannot establish causation of geometric errors. First observed dominance is not an acquisition time. [Evidence](<../outputs/stage6b/c1_dynamics/demand_coupling.json>).

Native geometry uses 666 manually reviewed intact discovery endpoints from 47 bases in 9 source groups. PC1/PC2 explain 36.1%/19.6% of discovery variance. Confirmation is projection-only; original 11-dimensional path metrics are also saved. Extraction covers 1766 manual-prefix, 18 other reviewed and 13122 conservative programmatic endpoints; 125216 unreviewed unresolved spans remain outside the labeled endpoint panel, and 292 traces have zero eligible endpoints. Sparse causal coverage prevents a cohort-level superiority claim for demand coupling. [Evidence](<../outputs/stage6b/trajectory/pca_discovery.json>).

In the frozen native traces, mask conditions average 8308 generated tokens versus 4738 for intact. 5/109 mask traces and 3/109 sham-mask traces reach the cap; all 109 intact traces finish with EOS. These are descriptive native adaptations, not causal failure-mode labels. [Native condition summary](<../outputs/stage6b/c1_mirage/native_condition_summary.json>).

C3 does not pass the full replication gate for sham-controlled target-VSD degradation or continuous divergence. There are 4 held-out mirage-like candidates. Across 63 present-object bases, native Yes answers number 61 for intact, 50 for strong, 41 for mask and 0 for no-image. Each condition uses its own native prefix; final-readout W2 does not measure earlier acquisition. Mask+yes is not automatically hallucination. One absent-reference yes remains an unresolved stools/chairs category boundary, and neither tested distractor shows the joint error-promoting direction. [Evidence](<../outputs/stage6b/c3_object_stress/replication_assessment.json>).

C4 reports matched passive effect sizes and individual cases only. In the 5 confirmation pairs, visual-mass/sink/entropy directions match the frozen controlled descriptor in 1/5, 2/5 and 3/5 pairs; all three mean-effect confidence intervals include zero. Its wrong-claim anchors do not provide the missing truth-oriented causal source contrasts. Global descriptor trends do not establish strict mirage, wandering or fixation replication. No natural cohort extension or new prevalence claim was made. [Cases and controls](<../outputs/stage6b/c4_natural_validation/individual_cases.md>).

Across 8 strict-candidate bases in 7 source groups, sink mass is lower than intact by a mean 0.0842. The signed candidate-minus-intact 95% bootstrap interval is[-0.1148, -0.0471]. After the declared discovery-only control for global visual mass and entropy, the signed mean is -0.0628, with interval[-0.0883, -0.0316]. These selected-case associations do not identify sink mediation or a causal behavioral prediction; the future-sink gate remains closed. [Sink statistics](<../outputs/stage6b/sink/sink_descriptive_statistics.json>).

Dataset and leave-one-dataset analyses preserve frozen thresholds. Grounding losses remain robust in every leave-one-dataset-out comparison. Attention divergence passes the secondary MathVision subgroup gate (19/21 positive bases, 13 source groups, Holm p=.0281), but not MathVerse/MathVista or any leave-one-dataset-out gate. Validated template-family labels are absent, so template-family robustness remains unidentified. No surrogate, rescue, training, representation substitution, head search or sink intervention was run.

##### Validation and execution limits

Exact native/no-op/passive controls, independent source arithmetic, frozen splits, readout orientation and mechanics-to-primary replay checks pass. BF16 weights and the canonical maximum 2048-token chunk/8-query barrier path are preserved. A long-prefix OOM required CPU residency for inactive caches and expandable allocator segments; the focused allocator comparison matched 18 common-prefix logits, and 10 long-context endpoints matched fresh canonical roots and all cached layers on both GPUs. Failed attempts remain available. [Audit](<../outputs/stage6b/audit/causal_score_replay.json>) · [Resources](<../outputs/stage6b/audit/resource_summary.json>).

Two cache-path exceptions are recorded in the resource audit: early Matplotlib imports may have used the default external cache, and pytest updated the project-root cache outside the allowed write list. Later plotting uses the allowed project cache, and the documented test reproduction command specifies an allowed cache directory. The existing pytest cache was left untouched after read-only verification; no external cache path was inspected or cleaned. [Cache audit](<../outputs/stage6b/audit/cache_configuration.json>).

##### Next stage

**GO — Cohort/Assay Repair.** Repair the primary dynamic demand/readout panel on the existing C1 cohort: resolve compound subgoals and obtain valid paired transition/hold and error-oriented readouts. This addresses an identification gap; retain all current negative and mixed findings. No failure class meets the 24-event rescue gate, C2 does not strongly establish alignment/retrieval dissociation, and natural sample size is not the main missing evidence. [One recommendation](<../outputs/stage6b/summaries/next_stage_recommendation.md>).

Stage6B stops here. #### Stage7A: Causal visual grounding states

**Complete. The approved question is whether a visual evidence claim can be distinguished by its causal source: the demanded source, an alternative or stale source, or insufficient visual support. Local extraction errors and later reasoning errors are assessed separately. Correct final answers, attention magnitude, and no-image agreement are not used as substitutes for causal grounding evidence.

The frozen classifier and statistical protocol produce the following records. The final assessment preserves class-level support for faithful reads and case-level support for rare failures.

| PRIOR_FILL | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| WRONG_SOURCE_READ | 3 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| STALE_SOURCE_READ | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| SOURCE_COUPLED_EXTRACTION_ERROR | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| DOWNSTREAM_INTEGRATION_ERROR | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 |

##### Value semantics and interpretation

Thirty-six unique assays cover the union of24 prespecified T controls and16 eligible weak states, with4 overlapping events. They patch semantic versus matched sham Values at fixed native routing/history in layers19–22. All self/no-op checks pass. Full-visual semantic-minus-sham is primary; ROI-only is secondary, because contextualized visual Values need not remain spatially local.

Within the16 weak states, all effects are positive; family median8.3125nats [7.1314,10.2163]. Discovery8 events/7 families: median9.6875 [7.4686,11.6875]; confirmation8/8:7.2238 [1.5000,14.2500]. T-only12/12 positive, median9.2812 [7.4218,12.9687]. ROI-only effects also positive16/16 (event median7.3933nats; secondary). Missing main265/main218/main743 are locally wrong claims requiring separate error-oriented controls; their semantics remain unresolved. The observed positives are locally correct eligible claims, not certified unfaithful failures or demonstrated correction opportunities. [Value summary](<../outputs/stage8a/analysis/value_v1/value_summary.json>), [semantic/sham figure](<../outputs/stage8a/analysis/value_v1/value_semantics.png>).

- **H1:** supported for selected MathVerse prefixes by held-out passive discrimination and eligible T causal validation.
- **H2:** a pure mention-only explanation is disfavored here, but annotation/source selection and absence of whole-trajectory evaluation limit generality.
- **H3:** uniform tight coupling is not established;9 held-out relative-weak states exist. Conversely, a relative quantile-defined state does not prove a natural bimodal failure regime.
- **H4:** supported at the eligible case level by retained Value semantics, but the required cohort size and deployable cheap gate are not achieved.

Counterfactual sensitivity does not establish that amplification of native Values improves accuracy, that extraction is intact for wrong claims, or that these events are MIRAGE/PRIOR_FILL. No intervention benefit was tested.

Frozen 2026-09-19T07:25:53.341356+00:00. **Selected interpretation: no broad outcome-level retrieval difference established under the full prespecified controls (Outcome D).** This is a failure to establish a robust broad difference, not evidence of equivalence or absence of local retrieval failures.

Wrong answers have more raw retrieval episodes and greater raw tortuosity. Length/completion adjustment alone retains several retrieval effects, so those effects cannot all be described as explained by length/capping. Adding the prespecified input controls attenuates count, density and mean movement; all eleven fully adjusted primary intervals and all within-family simultaneous intervals include zero. No primary family meets the frozen joint-evidence criterion. The recommendation below follows the already approved Block2 direction; no new research action is launched.

##### Cohort and frozen method

Exactly256 unique MathVision items/families from Block0:134 correct,105 wrong,17 unresolved. Scorable accuracy is134/239=56.07%; known-correct fraction of all256 is52.34%. No unresolved item is silently classified as wrong. Normal completions:133 correct/105 wrong (238); capped:1 correct/0 wrong/17 unresolved (18). The local outcome adapter does not reproduce upstream GPT-4o extraction. All contrasts use items,4000 stratified item-bootstrap resamples,seed1234 and float64 statistics. No token/episode pseudoreplication, local L labels, new model run or causal intervention.

Effects below are wrong minus correct. Full controls are log reasoning length, completion, pooled subject/subtype, answer format, log question length and categorical difficulty. These are descriptive adjustments; reasoning length/completion may themselves follow reasoning dynamics. Raw standardized effects are Hedges g; adjusted standardized effects and all additional intervals are in the JSON/CSV artifacts.

**Amount:** raw count difference is+3.44 episodes (95% CI0.63–6.20). It persists after length/completion controls (+3.64,0.66–6.56), but falls to+1.10 (−1.95–4.15) with full controls. Raw density and active fraction point in the opposite direction from count; they turn positive after length control. The full family does not establish a coherent amount difference.

**Timing/recurrence:** count and recurrence are algebraically related and cannot count as independent confirming constructs. Full recurrence is+0.95 (−2.06–3.96); first timing and late fractions do not provide a robust complementary contrast. The median-gap estimate remains negative (−117 tokens), but its full pointwise interval is−281 to+6 and its family interval is−310 to+76. Loss of precision alone does not establish that covariates explain this estimate.

**Geometry:** raw tortuosity differs by+1,155 (522–1,794), but length/completion-adjusted difference is+50 (−372–464). Transition-normalized movement is higher after length/completion controls (+0.0833,0.0346–0.1324) and attenuates with full controls (+0.0227,−0.0218–0.0690). There is no joint adjusted geometry finding to support a retrieval-instability or source-routing claim.

Thus H1 is not established under the complete control set; H2 has narrower length-only evidence for some metrics but not a robust full-adjustment phenotype; H3 is not established. Outcome E (all apparent differences explained by length/completion) is too strong for the observed count and movement results. Neither a causal explanation nor equivalence is established.

##### Robustness and limitations

Normal-completion raw differences remain: episode count+3.54 [0.70,6.19], tortuosity+1,177 [542,1,826]. Full normal-subset effects have the same point estimates as full all-scorable effects, up to numerical precision, and all their family intervals include zero. This is not independent confirmation: the only scorable capped item is correct, and its cap indicator isolates its contribution. There are no scored capped wrong items, so a within-cap outcome contrast is unavailable.

The frozen matching procedure yields64 correct/wrong pairs (128/239 scorable items). Standardized log-length imbalance decreases from0.580 to0.035; question-length imbalance from0.109 to−0.063. Matched count difference is+1.38 [−2.27,4.48], movement+0.00108 [−0.0529,0.0534], and tortuosity−33.6 [−625,498]. All primary matched intervals include zero. Matching conditions on selected pairs, with49 usable pairs for first/late timing and34 for median gap; it does not cover the entire cohort.

At gap0 and gap8, fully adjusted episode-count differences remain uncertain (+1.36 [−3.19,6.06] and+1.38 [−1.18,3.92]); recurrence and density are likewise uncertain. Gap0 median gap alone has a pointwise interval below zero (−110 [−266,−2.35]); gap4 and gap8 do not. Preserve this sensitivity result without promoting it into a broad finding. Removing the frozen low-displacement tail leaves tortuosity uncertain (+43.6 [−365,470]).

Timing is conditional on having enough detected episodes.32/134 correct and5/105 wrong items have no detected episode; first/late timing uses102/100 items, while median gap uses89/90. Missingness is reported, not imputed as no delay or no failure. Different group coverage, skewed distributions, heterogeneous inputs and finite sample uncertainty limit generalization. The detector measures passive retrieval activation, not a causal certificate of faithful reading.

##### Completion and phase analyses

Completion comparisons retain all17 unresolved items. Capped versus normal raw episode count is7.83 versus9.32; density0.191 versus1.525 per1000 tokens; active fraction0.000703 versus0.006604; mean movement0.905 versus1.039; tortuosity7,391 versus4,196. Capped lengths span40,179–40,960 tokens and normal lengths211–38,876: **there is no length-range overlap**. Full adjusted cap coefficients are retained for transparency, but reversal of density/active-fraction signs is model-dependent extrapolation, not evidence of a cap-specific mechanism or outcome effect. Small n=18 and outcome/completion imbalance are central limitations.

Both outcome groups concentrate retrieval early. Phase1 density averages4.323 correct versus3.971 wrong; phase4 averages0.280 versus0.240. All four fully adjusted density and active-fraction intervals cross zero. Some secondary pointwise mean-R effects are positive (phases1,2,4); early movement is+0.0610 [0.00250,0.1231]. Late-minus-early movement is−0.0568 [−0.0980,−0.0152]. These remain descriptive phase comparisons without multiplicity confirmation or causal-onset inference. Secondary global net displacement and the fraction after0.25 also have pointwise differences; neither replaces the primary family decision.

##### Exactly one recommendation for Block2

**Emphasize local-read success versus failure (L+ versus L−) at active task-required retrieval events in Block2, across both final-outcome groups, while retaining frozen event membership and eligibility.** Final-answer grouping did not yield a robust fully controlled phenotype and must not serve as a proxy for local visual-read correctness. This recommendation changes emphasis only; it does not select new events based on these contrasts. The Block2 protocol and local-read execution are not started in this action.

  not every visual error in a trajectory. No later error was substituted to
  increase failure yield. Twelve T readout anchors precede episode onset;
  onset/episode contrasts are concurrent descriptions, not validated predictors.

  The three affected localizable failures (2299,1833,2450) therefore remained
  unmatched under exact recorded strata, and were still replayed. Missing
  subtype metadata were not imputed after results opened. ROI-type granularity
  also varies across records. This restricts the matching interpretation.
- Full adjustment is unavailable: activation has31 design columns but only16
  L− families; routing has20 columns and rank17 with11 L− families. Matching
  does not establish balance on all nuisance variables. One pair crosses
  completion classes, and duration/length residual differences remain.
- Source sets contain only2–3 annotated regions. QK uses log-mean-exp to account
  for token count; raw attention share and transport still depend on ROI area.
  Source identity/localizability does not establish causal identifiability.
- All148 reviewed T claims have active retrieval within±32 tokens, and253/456
  selected events are M. Both are conditional on retrieval-selected membership.

  are unidentifiable; the100% conditional coverage is not population recall.
- Only three trajectories have multiple replayed anchors. Their candidate
  inventories change, so continuous lag, stale-source persistence, oscillation
  and comparable source-transition accuracy remain unavailable. Sparse exact-ROI

#### Stage 9A — completed; stop at the regime-validation gate

The proposed Thinking-specific recurrent visual-access regime is **not supported** in this 128-family native comparison. None of the four predeclared Thinking−CoT primary contrasts is positive at the required confidence. Thinking has fewer frozen-proxy episodes per 1,000 reasoning tokens; the other primary intervals include zero. Sparse matched-length and causal support prevents an equivalence conclusion. The secondary accuracy advantage does not establish the proposed mechanism.

**Exactly one recommendation:** Stop the Stage 9 bottleneck/bypass branch here and retain the existing reasoning-conditioned dynamic visual-retrieval framing. Execution stopped after the approved Stage 9A validation; no Stage 9B/C or other follow-on experiment was launched.

##### Execution and measurement

All 384 native trajectories are preserved: 128 per arm, 128 distinct conservative families from the unused MathVision reserve, 15 subjects, difficulty 1–5, 60 multiple-choice and 68 free-response items. The 2B Instruct/Thinking checkpoints used BF16, temperature 1, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, unchanged image preprocessing, and the 40,960-token cap. Direct and CoT share the Instruct template; only CoT appends the frozen instruction. Thinking retains its native `<think>` template. “Direct” means no added CoT instruction; it did not force short answers or suppress spontaneous reasoning.

All native artifact hashes were reverified. The detector, threshold 0.5478025980771918, layers 19–22 and max-over-head/layer aggregation were unchanged. First-token undefined detector/QK values are excluded. Primary native reasoning spans and common non-special full-assistant sensitivity are both reported. Bootstrap units are whole families, 4000 resamples; four primary 98.75% intervals, secondary 95%, minimum 20 contributing families.

| Arm | Mean / median reasoning tokens | Capped | Uncertain span boundaries | Reviewed demands / covered trajectories |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Direct | 15334 / 8553 | 34/128 | 52/128 | 176 / 77 |
| Prompted CoT | 11746 / 6188 | 24/128 | 51/128 | 181 / 74 |
| Thinking | 18493 / 14492 | 14/128 | 11/128 | 182 / 77 |

The frozen CoT instruction did not increase mean or median trace length relative to Direct in this cohort. This is a comparison of one approved prompting protocol with native Thinking, not evidence about every possible CoT elicitation method.

##### Primary paired contrasts

Effects below are Thinking minus prompted CoT. Each metric uses its actual paired overlap; missing demand annotations and no-episode denominators are not zero.

| Endpoint | Paired families | Thinking / CoT mean on paired support | Effect | 98.75% CI |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Demand alignment ±16 | 55 | 0.330 / 0.362 | -0.032 | [-0.203, 0.142] |
| Late episode fraction | 94 | 0.041 / 0.050 | -0.008 | [-0.055, 0.030] |
| Episodes / 1,000 tokens | 128 | 2.437 / 5.122 | -2.685 | [-4.533, -1.097] |
| Long-gap re-engagement | 94 | 0.140 / 0.113 | 0.027 | [-0.019, 0.069] |

The exploratory raw episode-count contrast is positive, while episodes per 1,000 tokens is negative. A greater total count in a longer trace is therefore insufficient evidence for the proposed recurrent regime. The common-assistant and normal-completion sensitivities preserve the negative density result. CoT−Direct primary-endpoint 95% intervals all include zero.

##### Length, demand specificity and raw routing controls

Only **9/128** same-item pairs satisfy the unchanged |Δlog length|≤.15 caliper. The matched endpoint supports are 4/7/9/7 families; no matched inferential interval is issued. No caliper widening or replacement pairing was used. Family-clustered OLS adjusts for arm, log length, completion, subject, difficulty, answer format and question length. These are adjusted associations: generated length/completion are post-checkpoint variables, not randomized controls.

| Adjusted Thinking−CoT coefficient | Effect | 98.75% CI | Families |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Demand alignment ±16 | 0.163 | [-0.032, 0.343] | 102 |
| Late episode fraction | 0.005 | [-0.032, 0.040] | 123 |
| Episodes / 1,000 tokens | 2.130 | [-0.437, 4.605] | 128 |
| Long-gap re-engagement | -0.014 | [-0.065, 0.037] | 123 |

All original regression designs have full column rank, and all 4000 bootstraps yield an identifiable Thinking−CoT coefficient; resampled category-rank losses are recorded. No adjusted primary interval is wholly positive.

539/700 explicit-demand nominations were accepted, 126 rejected and 35 unknown, after review of source images and local text. The 539 accepted events cover 102 distinct families and 228 trajectories; 114 trajectories had no nominated phrase. This is bounded explicit-phrase coverage, not an exhaustive demand census. All annotations were completed by the main Codex annotator, not independent human reviewers. Arm IDs, gold/correctness, routing and causal effects were masked; prose style can still reveal the arm.

| Arm | Demand ±16 | Circular-shift control | Demand minus shift, 95% CI |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Direct | 0.355 | 0.054 | 0.301 [0.205, 0.405] |
| Prompted CoT | 0.316 | 0.092 | 0.225 [0.137, 0.318] |
| Thinking | 0.368 | 0.039 | 0.329 [0.242, 0.418] |

Demand-associated retrieval exceeds circular-shift controls in all three arms, but its paired Thinking−CoT difference is 0.041, 95% CI [-0.101, 0.183]. It does not establish Thinking-specific demand alignment. Unpaired arm means above and paired P1 means differ because annotation overlap differs. Reviewed non-demand controls, onset-only alignment, ±32 windows and full-window edge sensitivities are retained. Non-demand paired support is particularly sparse; unknowns are never used as negative controls.

Raw visual attention/QK channels and continuous detector score are also lower for Thinking on the unadjusted family comparison. For example, the mean of the frozen max-aggregated visual-mass channel is 0.0787 versus 0.1134, and mean R is 0.2188 versus 0.2537 (Thinking/CoT). These are aggregation-specific observations, not calibrated probabilities of visual causality. Per-token spatial focus/entropy and reviewed target/donor/residual source-partition diagnostics accompany the detector. Spatial entropy is not labeled semantic-source entropy.

The negative density contrast persists in both answer formats and in every leave-one-subject-out mean (range −3.076 to −2.210 episodes/1,000). Fine problem-type, visual-density and entity-count metadata are unknown for all 128 items; those fields cannot establish robustness. Subject/category is the available problem-subtype proxy. Most individual subjects lack 20-family support.

##### Frozen causal validation

All **50/50** eligible events were replayed: Direct 16, CoT 16, Thinking 18, at most one event per family/arm. Selection used only reviewed demand, local source/readout eligibility and stable hashes before any measurements. All 610 source/readout nominations were reviewed; the final bounded inventory yielded 86 eligible demands before the one-family/arm selection. Numeric-boundary and ROI-coordinate repairs, and the rejection of an article mistaken for a vertex label, were preserved before the freeze.

Tests use the exact native token prefix and next local evidence string, with same-image different-content Values copied into either the demanded or irrelevant region at layers 19–22 under native selected-layer routing. Original versus donor-counterfactual strings are scored by mean token log probability. Positive effect means a donor-semantic preference shift. Self/sham must reproduce native logits exactly. This is source-local Value validation, not a pixel counterfactual or an all-path visual-causality test.

| Arm | Events | Target effect | Irrelevant effect | Target−irrelevant | Positive target−irrelevant events |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Direct | 16 | 3.15488 | 0.00510 | 3.14978 | 16 |
| Prompted CoT | 16 | 2.25032 | -0.01097 | 2.26129 | 15 |
| Thinking | 18 | 3.11974 | 0.03282 | 3.08692 | 18 |

The paired Thinking−CoT target-minus-irrelevant effect is 0.74995 across 12 overlapping families; CI: not estimable (<20 families). All arm-specific samples fall below both the 24-event feasibility aim and 20-family inference threshold. These results cannot establish a robust causal arm difference. Eligibility is limited to the implemented clear discrete-content assay, not all possible visual events.

Pooling arms with equal family weight gives target-minus-irrelevant 2.85239, 95% CI [2.06815, 3.65862], across 26 families. This pooled validation does not test Thinking specificity. Native-prefix passive features are exact in 50/50 events; maximum absolute difference 0.0. Capture and self/sham logits are exact at every scored query; sham semantic effects are exactly zero. The raw FP64 JS expression leaves at most 5.50e-17 signed roundoff; raw values are preserved, with a 64-machine-epsilon aggregation tolerance and unchanged mandatory exact-logit/score checks. Optional alphaV/post-WO and source-selectivity measurements are saved on these 50 first queries only.

Donors retain their native positional/contextual information. Irrelevant controls match token shape/cardinality and minimize ink; they are not Value-norm or visual-content matched. Original and counterfactual strings are teacher-forced from the same original prefix. At each query, every intervention uses the same unperturbed history for that candidate; intervention-altered caches do not propagate. Final-answer accuracy never substitutes for the local readout.

##### Secondary accuracy

All 384 extractions received masked review. The unchanged local Qwen/MathVision adapter uses bounded numeric equivalence at 1e−6 and no external judge. Formatting/units and superseded intermediate answers were corrected by literal text review before gold comparison. Raw-adapter scores remain available. Unscorable cases receive no credit in the all 128 denominator and remain distinct from known wrong answers.

| Arm | Reviewed correct / wrong / unscorable | All-example accuracy | Scorable-only accuracy | Raw-adapter all-example accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Direct | 32 / 66 / 30 | 25.00% | 32.65% | 13.28% |
| Prompted CoT | 38 / 68 / 22 | 29.69% | 35.85% | 19.53% |
| Thinking | 58 / 57 / 13 | 45.31% | 50.43% | 40.62% |

Thinking−CoT reviewed no-credit accuracy is +15.63 percentage points (secondary 95% paired CI +7.03 to +23.44). Accuracy is a separate outcome and does not override the failed primary regime gate.

##### Decision gates and stopping boundary

| Required criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| At least two positive primary Thinking−CoT effects | Not met: 0/4 |
| At least one survives length control | Not established; 9 matched pairs, all adjusted primary CIs include zero |
| Demand-specific re-engagement | Supported within arms; Thinking-specific advantage not established |
| Causal support for part of the arm difference | Insufficient eligible independent support |
| Not driven by one subtype | No positive primary phenotype to certify; negative density broad across available categories |

This is a negative result for advancing the proposed native-regime story, with unresolved matching/causal precision and incomplete fine-subtype coverage. It does not show computational equivalence, absence of visual retrieval, absence of all Thinking advantages, or the cause of the accuracy difference. No additional benchmark, prompt, threshold or model was tried to rescue the hypothesis.

Native trajectories contain 5,976,205 generated tokens and 70.24 measured inference GPU-hours. Causal event execution adds 1.40 GPU-hours, excluding model startup, with peak allocated VRAM 19.60 GiB. GPU workers 121562/121563/121564 used one A6000 each on node06. CPU-only 121568 ran on node03 for 9m 02s; pending CPU-only 121566 was cancelled before work and moved due host-memory capacity. Slurm accounting storage is disabled, so measured runtimes and captured job/worker receipts are retained instead of an invented billing total. Annotation burden: 700 semantic nominations, 610 local source/readout nominations, 128 source images, 50 sets of source/donor/control crops, and 384 answer extractions; no human annotation-hour estimate.

The native generation config is preserved. `stage9a_generation_config_node07.json` is the actual execution-config identity after the documented resource amendment; its scientific settings match the original. All workers release allocations when their bounded queues end; final release status is in `audit/final_validation.json`.
